 Gold (XAU/INR) Price Forecast in India: 2026, 2027 and Next 5 Years Predictions (INR per troy ounce) Jana Kane https://www.litefinance.org/blog/authors/jana-kane/ Today, 19.11.2026, gold (XAU/INR) trades at ₹346,692.40 per troy ounce, a -4.09% change over the past year. Below is our gold price prediction for India: a monthly gold rate forecast for 2026–2028, the outlook for the next 5 years and 2030, plus the gold rate history in India and the local factors that move it. You will also find a short-term view: whether the gold rate may increase or decrease in the coming days, and what the model shows for next month.

 Major Takeaways (as of November 2026)
 Here is the short version of our gold rate forecast for India:
 Current price: gold (XAU/INR) trades at ₹346,692.40 per troy ounce. For the price per 10 grams of 24 carat gold, divide by 3.11.
 All-time high: XAU/INR peaked at ₹515,993.32 on 29.01.2026.
 2026 forecast: we expect the gold rate in India to move between ₹282,138.58 and ₹405,222.36 per troy ounce for the rest of the year.
 Coming days: the daily technical signal for XAU/INR is Strong buy. The model's range for the current month is ₹346,272.23–₹392,787.94 per troy ounce.
 Next 5 years: the projected range is ₹321,948.38–₹373,074.30 per troy ounce.
 Main local driver: the USD/INR rate. A weaker Indian rupee pushes the gold rate in India up even when XAU/USD stays flat.
 Gold Real-Time Market Overview (XAU/INR)
 Gold ( XAU/INR ) now trades at ₹346,692.40 per troy ounce, -0.72% over the past 24 hours and -11.95% over the past month. The rupee price is built from two quotes: the global gold price in US dollars, currently $3,707.14 per troy ounce, multiplied by the USD/INR rate. To switch to the unit Indian buyers use, divide the ounce price by 31.1035 and multiply by 10: that gives the price per 10 grams of 24 carat gold before taxes. For 22 carat gold, multiply the 24 carat figure by 0.9167. For the price per gram, divide the ounce price by 31.1.
 Local quotes such as the IBJA rate and MCX gold sit above this figure. Since May 13, 2026, India charges a 15% import duty on gold (10% basic customs duty plus 5% AIDC), and buyers pay 3% GST on top. Jewellery also comes with making charges, taxed at 5% GST.
 Will the Gold Rate Increase or Decrease in the Coming Days in India?
 No model can call the next few sessions with certainty, so we rely on readings that update every day. Here is what they show for XAU/INR right now:
 Daily technical signal: Strong buy.
 Support levels: ₹346,272.23. If the price falls, these are the first areas where buyers may step in.
 Resistance levels: ₹374,318.68. A rise has to pass them to continue.
 Trader sentiment: 59.99% of LiteFinance traders hold positions in the direction: Sell.
 Volatility over 30 days: +50.00%. The higher it is, the wider the daily swings in rupees.
 Will the gold rate decrease in the coming days?
 The gold rate in India usually decreases in three cases. The US dollar strengthens and global gold falls, as it does when markets expect higher US interest rates. The rupee gains against the dollar. Or local demand cools after Diwali, before the wedding season picks up. Over the past month, XAU/INR has changed by -11.95%, and the all-time high now stands 48.83% above the current price.
 How much can the gold rate decrease?
 The nearest reference points are the support levels listed above. Beyond them, the model's low for the current month is ₹346,272.23, the low for the rest of 2026 is ₹282,138.58, and the low for 2027 is ₹321,948.38 per troy ounce. To see what that means for 10 grams of 24 carat gold, divide by 3.11.
 When will the gold price increase in India?
 Gold in rupees tends to rise when the Fed cuts interest rates, when the rupee weakens against the dollar and when investors look for a safe haven. Inside India, jewellers restock before Akshaya Tritiya, Dhanteras and the wedding season, which adds to local premiums. The model's upper bound is ₹405,222.36 for the rest of 2026 and ₹366,532.03 for 2027.
 Gold Rate Prediction for Next Week in India
 For the week ahead, the weekly Ichimoku reading for XAU/INR points to: downward. The chart shows the expected price path for the next 7 days.
 Traders who work on the weekly timeframe can use these reference levels:
 Entry level: ₹402,637.03.
 Take profit: ₹456,672.21.
 Stop loss: ₹343,198.33.
 Within one week, the gold rate in India reacts mostly to US inflation and jobs data, Fed speeches and moves in USD/INR. Local demand changes more slowly, so it rarely decides the direction of a single week.
 Gold Rate Prediction for Next Month and Next 6 Months in India
 The chart below shows the gold rate prediction for next month: the expected XAU/INR path over the coming 30 days.
 The exact figures are in the monthly tables that follow. The 2026 table starts with next month and gives its minimum, average and maximum price per troy ounce. For a gold rate prediction for the next 6 months in India, read six rows in a row: the months left in 2026, then the first months of 2027.
 Over a six-month window, three things move the price most: Fed and RBI rate decisions, the Union Budget in early February, when import duty can change, and the festival and wedding seasons. The 90-day chart covers the first half of that window.
 Gold Price Forecast for 2026 in India
 Our gold price prediction for 2026 in India covers the months left until the end of the year. The table shows the expected minimum, average and maximum XAU/INR rate per troy ounce for each month.
 Date Minimum, ₹ Average Price, ₹ Maximum, ₹

 For the rest of 2026, the gold rate forecast for India puts XAU/INR between ₹282,138.58 and ₹405,222.36, with an average of ₹348,743.63. Over 2026 as a whole, the price is expected to change by -11.74%.
 The end of the year is a busy season for the Indian gold market. Demand peaks around Dhanteras and Diwali and stays firm through the wedding season. On top of that, the 15% import duty keeps the gold rate in India above the international price converted at the USD/INR rate.
 Highest and Lowest Gold Rate in 2026 in India
 Over the past 52 weeks, XAU/INR has traded in the range ₹2,836.93 – ₹515,993.32. The all-time high is ₹515,993.32, set on 29.01.2026. For the months left in 2026, the model's maximum is ₹405,222.36 and the minimum is ₹282,138.58 per troy ounce.

 A few dates on the 2027 calendar can move the price. The first to watch is the Union Budget in early February, the usual moment for changes to import duty and GST rules on gold, and any cut or hike shows up in local prices almost at once. Akshaya Tritiya in spring and the wedding season tend to lift physical demand. All year long, Fed rate decisions and RBI policy move the US dollar and the Indian rupee, and that shifts XAU/INR even when the dollar price of gold barely moves.

 Three forces matter most on this horizon. Central bank buying, including the RBI adding to India's gold reserves, supports demand worldwide. Over the long run, the Indian rupee has kept weakening against the US dollar, and every step down adds to the gold rate in India. A growing share of Indian investors also buy gold ETFs and digital gold instead of jewellery, so demand becomes less seasonal and more tied to market moves.

 Will the gold rate increase or decrease in future? A five-year path never runs in a straight line, and gold has seen double-digit corrections even in strong bull cycles. Over this horizon, the direction will mostly come from three things: how the Fed and RBI move interest rates, how much gold central banks keep buying, and where USD/INR goes. A softer rupee alone can lift the gold rate in India in years when the global price stalls.
 Gold Rate in 2030 in India and Long-Term Outlook to 2035
 What will the gold rate in 2030 in India be? Our model puts XAU/INR between ₹325,036.96 and ₹373,074.30 per troy ounce. Further out, the 2035 forecast ranges from ₹329,954.39 to ₹377,831.53.
 This far ahead, a single number means little, so it makes more sense to think in scenarios:
 Bullish : inflation stays sticky, central banks keep adding gold and the rupee keeps sliding. The gold price in 2030 in India moves toward the top of the range.
 Base : interest rates settle, demand from India and China holds steady, and gold grows roughly in line with inflation plus the rupee's depreciation. The price stays near the middle of the range.
 Bearish : real interest rates rise, the US dollar strengthens and safe haven demand fades. XAU/INR drifts toward the lower bound, although a weaker rupee softens the drop for Indian buyers.
 What Drives Gold Prices in India
 The gold rate in India follows the global market, but local factors decide how much buyers actually pay. Here are the five that matter most:
 USD/INR exchange rate. Gold is bought abroad in dollars, so the rupee's value decides how much Indians pay. When the Indian rupee weakens, the gold rate in India rises even if XAU/USD stays flat, and a stronger rupee works the other way.
 RBI policy and gold reserves. The Reserve Bank of India 's repo rate is now 5.50%. Lower rates make gold more attractive compared with fixed deposits, while the RBI's own purchases for India's gold reserves add to demand.
 Import duty and GST. India imports almost all the gold it uses, so taxes go straight into the price. The current 15% import duty plus 3% GST explains most of the gap between the local rate and the international price.
 Seasonal demand. Buying picks up around Dhanteras and Diwali, on Akshaya Tritiya and during the wedding season. Jewellers stock up ahead of these dates, which often lifts local premiums. Record prices cut into this: the World Gold Council expects India's gold demand in 2026 to fall to about 650 tonnes, the lowest since 2020.
 Global factors. Fed rate decisions move the US dollar and gold worldwide. With the US rate at +3.88% and XAU/USD at $3,707.14, every Fed meeting can shift the gold rate prediction for India.

 Forecasting Methodology
 Our gold price forecast for India combines two models: a forecast for XAU/USD and a forecast for the USD/INR exchange rate. Multiplying them gives the expected XAU/INR price per troy ounce. Local rates also include the 15% import duty and 3% GST, so retail prices in India will sit above these figures.

 Gold Rate Prediction in India: FAQ
 Will the gold rate decrease in India? Short-term dips are always possible. The gold price in India can decrease if the rupee strengthens, the Fed keeps interest rates high or the government cuts the import duty. Our model expects the low for 2027 at ₹321,948.38 per troy ounce, so a drop is part of the forecast, not a reversal of the long-term trend.
 What is the gold rate prediction for next 5 years in India? Over the next five years, we expect XAU/INR to trade within ₹321,948.38–₹373,074.30 per troy ounce, with the price near ₹344,091.21 by December 2031.
 Is it a good time to buy gold in India now? That depends on your horizon. For traders, the current daily signal is Strong buy, with support at ₹346,272.23 and resistance at ₹374,318.68. Long-term buyers often spread purchases over time instead of trying to catch the bottom.
 Why is gold more expensive in India than the international price? India imports almost all its gold, so the local rate includes a 15% import duty and 3% GST on top of the global price converted from US dollars. Jewellery adds making charges with 5% GST, which widens the gap further.
